answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy comes from binding each voting or mining identity to a bond that is slashed on proven duplication, so a single operator running many wallets pays the full bond for every fake identity instead of one fee split across dozens. Detection compounds the cost: linked wallets revealed by shared funding, timing, or repeated attestation patterns trigger cascading slashes that freeze the whole cluster at once. The result is a whisper of profit replaced by a river of collateral at risk, and only an honest kernel of independent operators survives the sieve.
